label: input token e at the start of the original sequence (steps 0-2)
explanation: Fires only when the input token is the letter e during the first few steps of the original phase. Activation is near max when e is the very first token (t=0, ~61% of mass), somewhat weaker at t=1 (~0.4-0.8 of max), weak at t=2 (~0.05-0.3 of max), and rare/weak at t=3; never fires at t>=4, at the delimiter, or in the copy phase (even when e is fed back as input). Never fires on any other token. A repeated e (e.g. second e in "e e ...") is weaker (~0.43 of max). Predicate (in_tok==e)&(t<=2) gives dev F1 0.91, mass recall 0.99; false positives are mostly e at t=2 that stay silent.

issues: The t=2 piece is noisy: (e & t==2) has precision 0.59 and holds about 9% of the activation mass. That is where all 6850 test false positives are. I checked whether a split by previous token (digit vs letter, vowel), digits seen earlier, or L could separate the firing cases from the silent ones. None did: precision stayed between 0.39 and 0.62 in every split. This looks like a weak, near-threshold tail rather than a missing rule.

The test misses (1752 steps, 0.6% of mass) are all e at t=3 with activation 0.03-0.15 of max. This matches the explanation's 'fires rarely and weakly at t=3'. Widening the predicate to t<=3 lowers F1 to 0.81.

Claims confirmed on test: e at t=0 has precision 1.0 and mass share 0.61. e at t=1 has precision 1.0. Zero activation at t>=4, at the delimiter and in the copy phase (e & phase!=0 never fires). in_tok is e for 100% of the activation mass. A repeated e at t=1 is about 0.43 of max in the examples.
